title: The Bosphorus Brief — 30 September 2026
overview: A quiet news day for daily life in Türkiye is anchored by one significant legal story: the ECtHR's latest mass ruling against Ankara over post-coup terrorism convictions. Elsewhere, an Iranian airliner's seizure at Istanbul Airport made headlines, Montenegro moved to end visa-free travel for Turkish citizens, and the lira continues to soften.

sections.heading: ECtHR Deals Turkey Another Major Rebuke
sections.body: The European Court of Human Rights has found violations in 947 more cases tied to post-coup terrorism convictions, adding to a long series of rulings against Ankara on this issue. For foreign residents and dual nationals with any connection to these prosecutions, the rulings reinforce that credible international review of due-process concerns continues, though they do not by themselves change individual case outcomes. Coverage of this story so far comes primarily from opposition-leaning Turkish Minute; watch for whether state-aligned outlets address the ruling in coming days.

sections.heading: Iranian Airliner Grounded Over Debt at Istanbul Airport
sections.body: A Caspian Airlines Boeing 737 was pulled from departure at Istanbul Airport after passengers had already boarded, reportedly over an unpaid debt of roughly €3 million. Passengers were ordered off before takeoff. International outlets (Euronews) and opposition-leaning Turkish Minute both covered the seizure with similar factual detail; no political framing has emerged. For travelers on Iranian carriers through Istanbul, it's a reminder that commercial disputes can occasionally disrupt flights with little warning — worth building buffer time into connections.

sections.heading: Montenegro to End Visa-Free Travel for Turkish Citizens
sections.body: Starting November 1, Montenegro will end visa-free entry for Turkish passport holders, part of a wider move affecting Russia and Belarus as well. Pro-government Türkiye Today and regional outlet Caspian Post both confirm the change. Turkish citizens with travel, property, or business plans in Montenegro should check visa requirements well ahead of the deadline; this does not affect foreign residents in Türkiye holding other passports.

sections.heading: Lira and Reserves Under Continued Pressure
sections.body: The Turkish lira remains soft, trading near 49.0 to the dollar and 55.7 to the euro, while the central bank's reserves fell by $4.3 billion amid what turkishminute.com describes as ongoing fund turmoil. A second individual has reportedly been arrested in a fraud scandal linked to a lira "signatory." For residents budgeting in foreign currency or transferring funds, the trend is worth watching, though no acute disruption is reported today.

sections.heading: Steady Ground: Earthquakes and Travel Levels Unchanged
sections.body: Recent M4+ tremors near Hilvan and Saimbeyli in the past week are consistent with Türkiye's normal seismic background and have not prompted new advisories. The US State Department's travel levels for the region remain unchanged, with Türkiye at Level 2 and neighboring Syria, Iraq, Iran, and Lebanon at Level 4. No new safety concerns for residents have emerged today.

closing: Steady as she goes — see you tomorrow with more.
